response:
It takes a lot of courage to honestly reflect on your relationship with alcohol and how it affects your emotions. Feeling a lingering sense of guilt after drinking, even when nothing objectively wrong happens, is a heavy burden to carry. This guilt might be your mind's way of signaling that your current drinking habits no longer align with your values or the person you want to be, especially given the distress it has caused in the past. 

While only a healthcare professional can determine if you have a clinical problem, experiencing personality changes like anger and carrying persistent guilt are very valid reasons to reevaluate your relationship with alcohol. You don't have to figure this out alone. Consider speaking with a therapist or counselor. They can help you explore the root of this anger and guilt in a safe, non-judgmental space, and support you in finding the healthiest path forward for your well-being.
